items.name: S&P 500 (VFV + SPY)
items.street: Strategists are split: earnings are still growing, but the market is leaning on a handful of AI names while yields and oil stay high.
items.take: Crowd mood on the S&P 500 is about as gloomy as it gets, while the index itself has barely pulled back. Your VFV and SPY move together, so this is the sentiment that matters most for you.

bears: Capex of $195–205B this year has pushed free cash flow negative
Debt and equity raising to fund AI build-out

bulls: Google Cloud grew 82% last quarter with a $514B backlog
TPU chips are seen as a $100B+ opportunity and a challenge to Nvidia
Stock looks oversold (RSI near 30) at about 24x forward earnings
items.name: Alphabet
items.street: Strong Buy from 62 analysts; average target about $421–431, roughly a third above Friday's $317 close. Q3 consensus: revenue about $127.5B (+25%), EPS about $3.
items.take: The crowd is divided into two camps: a Cloud blowout sends it higher, a capex hike sends it lower. Your call is about $13 below its $330 strike, so the Oct 28 reaction matters a lot for its value.

items.name: Amazon
items.street: Strong Buy from 60 analysts; average target about $331, about a third above Friday's $248 close. The number everyone is watching is AWS growth (30–35% expected).
items.take: Retail traders are more upbeat on Amazon than on Alphabet going into earnings. Your call is about $12 below its $260 strike; AWS growth vs. the 30–35% range is the swing factor.

mood.summary: Investors are nervous. The Fear & Greed index has sat in Extreme Fear for two weeks, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 9 points, well below the long-run norm. The S&P 500 fell for a second week and is about 2.5% off its Oct 6 record, while the Nasdaq is about 6% off after its worst day since June on Oct 22. Worries centre on AI spending, oil above $110 on Middle East tensions, and a possible Fed hike in December. Very fearful readings have often come before rebounds, but they don't say when.

items.name: Intel
items.about: Designs and manufactures x86 processors and runs a contract chip-making (foundry) business.
items.why: Shares fell about 29% from $92.07 to $65.04 on heavy volume the session after Intel's results, the day's biggest decliner on the board. Posts say the drop was about a revenue miss and PC-chip weakness, but that is unconfirmed; the sell-off spread to other chip names.

items.name: Invesco QQQ Trust
items.about: Tracks the Nasdaq-100 index of large non-financial companies, weighted toward technology.
items.why: The fund fell 3.5% to $690.23, its worst day in a while, as chip and AI-linked stocks sold off after Intel's results. It recovered part of the loss into the close; posts say traders are watching whether $700 is reclaimed on Monday.

items.name: Sandisk
items.about: Makes NAND flash memory and solid-state drives for data centers, PCs and phones.
items.why: Shares dropped 13.6% to $1,149 in the chip rout, though they were well off the low of $1,115 by the close. Posts say traders are looking to Apple's results on Monday for memory-demand commentary; that is crowd speculation.

items.name: Reddit
items.about: Operates the Reddit social platform and sells advertising and data licenses.
items.why: Shares fell 29% to $91.78 from $129.60, extending a slide that posts date back to its earnings report and say had already taken the stock from the $150s. Posts also point to worries about slowing ad revenue across large platforms and to insider selling, which are unconfirmed.

items.name: CorMedix
items.about: Commercial-stage drugmaker; its DefenCath catheter-lock solution is used in dialysis.
items.why: Shares fell 25.5% to a fresh 52-week low of $5.69 after DaVita warned of a sharp drop in 2027 DefenCath reimbursement, according to a Stocktwits News report linked in the stream. Posts also cite a CMS add-on payment of $8.322 per treatment for Q1 2027 and about 20% short interest.

items.name: TG Therapeutics
items.about: Biopharma company marketing Briumvi, a treatment for relapsing multiple sclerosis.
items.why: Shares rose 5.4% to $61.19 while the market fell. Posts say shorts were squeezed and point to upcoming Q3 results and a Phase 3 readout for a subcutaneous formulation; no company news was cited, so the catalyst is unconfirmed.

items.name: Iovance Biotherapeutics
items.about: Cell-therapy company selling Amtagvi for advanced melanoma and Proleukin.
items.why: Shares fell 11.8% to $8.44 after lung-cancer data on Thursday; posts say the 69-patient NSCLC group showed a 24.6% response rate, with stronger results in biomarker subsets but immature duration data. Posts also speculate about a buyout, which is unconfirmed.

items.name: Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X
items.about: Seeks three times the daily return of a semiconductor index, so moves are amplified in both directions.
items.why: The 3x fund fell 25% to $76.60 on a day semiconductor stocks sold off, with record-level share volume of about 184 million per posts. It bounced roughly 8% off the $70.24 low by the close.

items.name: Lumentum
items.about: Makes lasers and optical components used in data-center networking and telecom.
items.why: Shares fell 8.7% to $840 in the chip sell-off. Posts say Marvell may be set to announce a deal for the company, possibly on Monday; this is unconfirmed and no announcement was cited.

items.name: SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF
items.about: Tracks the 30-stock Dow Jones Industrial Average.
items.why: The Dow ETF fell 1.1% to $516.78, a milder drop than the Nasdaq ETF's 3.5%, in a broad Friday selloff led by chips after Intel's results. Posts show traders split on whether Monday brings a rebound.

items.name: AppLovin
items.about: Ad-tech company whose AI-driven platform matches advertisers with mobile apps and games.
items.why: Shares fell 10.4% to $228.47, hitting lows after drifting down through the session. Posts say the move is tied to worries about slowing ad revenue at other large platforms; that is unconfirmed.

items.name: ProShares Ultra VIX Short-Term Futures ETF
items.about: A leveraged fund tied to short-term VIX futures, used to bet on rising market volatility.
items.why: The fund jumped 16% to $19.44 as the VIX rose with Friday's stock selloff, then pared gains late in the day. Such funds usually decay over time, which posts note.

items.name: SELLAS Life Sciences
items.about: Clinical-stage biotech developing the cancer drug candidate galinpepimut-S.
items.why: Shares slipped 4.6% to $9.69 in a down market. Posts say holders are waiting for trial results they expect soon; no company news was cited, so any catalyst is unconfirmed.

items.name: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals
items.about: Biotech company behind Eylea and, with Sanofi, Dupixent.
items.why: Shares rose 13.3% to $927.67 after quarterly results. A news link in the stream says Dupixent sales drove the earnings and a margin upgrade, with US sales topping $5 billion.

items.name: ProShares UltraPro QQQ
items.about: Seeks three times the daily return of the Nasdaq-100, so moves are amplified.
items.why: The 3x fund fell 10.6% to $61.90, about three times the Nasdaq-100 ETF's 3.5% drop, as tech stocks sold off. Posts show dip-buyers and traders eyeing a Monday rebound.

items.name: Gorilla Technology
items.about: Provides AI-driven video analytics and security software and network infrastructure.
items.why: Shares fell 17.8% to $7.51. Posts say the company is raising about $111.1 million, close to 40% of its market value, which would dilute holders; the figure is unconfirmed here.

items.name: NVIDIA
items.about: Designs GPUs and systems that power AI data centers, gaming and graphics.
items.why: Shares fell 4.2% to $204.70 as chip stocks sold off after Intel's results, recovering from a low of $200.93. Posts say the stock finished back above its 200-day average.

items.name: Carnival
items.about: The world's largest cruise operator, with brands including Carnival, Princess and Holland America.
items.why: Shares ended flat at $28.85 on a day the Nasdaq ETF fell 3.5%. Posts note the resilience and mention a data-breach notice and a ship refit, but no clear catalyst was cited.

items.name: Alphabet (Class C)
items.about: Parent of Google, with search, YouTube, Google Cloud and Waymo.
items.why: Shares fell 1.3% to $278.59, a much milder drop than the Nasdaq ETF's, though still about 12% below the Oct 27 close of $317.30 after the company's results. Posts discuss its TPU chips and say dip-buyers are active.

items.name: iShares Semiconductor ETF
items.about: Holds a basket of US-listed semiconductor companies.
items.why: The fund fell 8.4% to $470.79, hitting $460.11 before recovering, as chip stocks sold off after Intel's results. Posts show traders split on whether the bounce holds on Monday.
